messages.author: f5989a05baac184d
messages.subject: use of I() within occ()
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if anyone else has had problems with the predict function when including a variable that is calculated with the I() function. I can plot the marginal effects of start_date_j but none of the other variables like min, noise, moon, or sky. The coefficients and standard errors look reasonable.

I can work around this problem by calculating the value (start_date_j2) outside of the occu function and inputting that as a separate site covariate (the results are identical), but I'd like to be able to quickly plot the marginal of start_date_j as a quadratic.

I ran into the same problem when trying to calculate the values using the predict function where all of the predicted values are NA with p.global.

site.stacked$start_date_j2 <- scale(site.stacked$start_date_j)*scale(site.stacked$start_date_j)


plotEffects with p.global2 works. 


predict with p.global2 also works.

Thanks!
Marie

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: use of I() within occ()
parts:
For future reference, the issue was that the model formula included a term like  + I(scale(x)^2) in which scale() was nested inside I(). This works fine for fitting the model but it will not work properly with predict(). I need to look into this more but I believe it is a limitation of R's model.matrix function and not unmarked specifically. 

A few possible workarounds:
(1) scale or calculate the squared term manually (or possibly do both) before making your unmarked frame. 
(2) Swap the order of scaling and squaring - i.e., square first, then scale.  In the formula:  scale(I(x^2)). This will result in different coefficient estimates, but in my experience, it will usually capture the same pattern in the data.
(3) If you don't need to use predict, or are OK to do the prediction calculations manually, you can use the original formula structure, as the model fitting itself works fine.

Ken
